newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Merchant share suspension to be lifted.
newsitem.headline: Merchant share suspension to be lifted.

text.p: The Colombo Stock Exchange said on Thursday it would lift on Friday the trading suspension imposed on shares in Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka Ltd (MBSL).
The exchange suspended the shares earlier on Thursday at the request of the bank, after the Controller of Exchange fined it 139 million rupees for a foreign exchange violation.
"We believe a one-day suspension is sufficient for the information to be disseminated in the market place," said an exchange official, who declined to be identified.

In a letter to the exchange MBSL asked for a suspension until further notice, saying it feared serious consequences to the bank and its shareholders before action could be initiated to have the Exchange Controller's order and penalty annulled.
Brokers agreed that the suspension should not continue indefinitely as requested by MBSL.
The suspension should only be in force until the information is disseminated in the market place, which should then be free to react, they said.
The controller said the fine was imposed on Merchant Bank for violating Sri Lanka's Exchange Control Act during the sale of 51 percent of Kotagala Plantations Ltd in 1995.
MBSL shares last traded at 15 rupees on Wednesday.
